1  THIS MFA FILED U/S 173(1) OF MV ACT AGAINST THE  JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 02.04.2018 PASSED IN MVC  NO.977/2017 ON THE FILE OF THE II ADDITIONAL DISTRICT  JUDGE AND MACT AT TUMAKURU, PARTLY ALLOWING THE  -2-  MFA No. 8534 of 2018 CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT 1.

In respect of an accident which is not in dispute and the liability of the insurer to pay the compensation is also not in dispute, the Tribunal has awarded the following sums as compensation:
Sl. Compensation under Amount in No. different Heads (Rs.)

1 . Pain and sufferings Rs.35,000/-
2.

Medical expenses Rs.78,145/-
3. Food and nourishment Rs.15,000/-
4. Transportation charges Rs.15,000/-
5. Loss of amenities in life Rs.25,000/-
6. Attendant charges Rs.5,500/-
Loss of income during laid 7. Rs.24,000/-
up period 8. Loss of future income Rs.1,72,800/-

9. Future medical expenses Rs.20,000/-
TOTAL Rs.3,90,445/-

2. The Tribunal has assessed the disability to the whole body at 10% and fixed the notional income at Rs.8,000/-
per month.
The treated Doctor who was examined has stated that the claimant had sustained the disability to the right lower limb at 39% and the whole body at 13%.
In the light of this clear evidence, the Tribunal ought not to have reduced the disability to 10%.
Consequently, it is held that the claimant has suffered disability to the extent of 13%.

3. So far as notional income is concerned, since, the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority has fixed Rs.11,000/- as the income for the accident of the year 2017, it would be appropriate to apply the said income as against Rs.8,000/-.
4. As the claimant was aged 20 years, a multiplier of '18' would have to be applied.
Consequently, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.3,08,880/- (Rs.11,000/- x 12 x 18 x 13%) towards 'loss of future income'.

5. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.35,000/- towards 'pain and sufferings' and Rs.25,000/-
towards 'loss of amenities in life'.
In my view, it would be appropriate to award a sum of Rs.50,000/- towards 'pain and sufferings' and Rs.40,000/- towards 'loss of amenities in life'.
6. The sum of Rs.78,145/- awarded towards 'medical expenses' and Rs.20,000/- awarded towards 'future medical expenses' are just and proper and are affirmed.

7. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.35,500/- (Rs.15,000/- + Rs.Rs.5,500 + Rs.15,000/-)
towards 'transportation charges, attendant charges and food and nourishment'.
Since, the claimant was hospitalized for 11 days, the said awards are just and proper and do not require any enhancement.
8. The Tribunal has treated the laid up period as three months.

Since, the income is now determined at Rs.11,000/-, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.33,000/- (Rs.11,000/- x 3) as against Rs.24,000/- awarded by the Tribunal towards 'loss of income during laid up period'.

9. Consequently, the award of the Tribunal is modified and the claimant would be entitled to the following compensation:

Thus, the claimant is held entitled to a total compensation of Rs.5,65,525/- as against Rs.3,90,445/-, along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
11. The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded within two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
The appeal is accordingly allowed in part.
